title: Sin as Missing the Mark
definition: The doctrine of Sin as Missing the Mark teaches that sin falls short of the glory, purpose, and righteousness for which God made humanity.
summary: Sin as Missing the Mark names a real biblical truth, not a religious slogan. sin falls short of the glory, purpose, and righteousness for which God made humanity. It helps believers understand the human condition, God’s promise, and the need to respond to the Lord with honesty and faith.
christFocus: Christ is central to Sin as Missing the Mark because He is the Savior who tells the truth about sin, judgment, weakness, and spiritual darkness while also providing the only lasting hope. In Him, God’s truth does not crush the repentant; it leads them to mercy, cleansing, freedom, and life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on this specific truth: sin falls short of the glory, purpose, and righteousness for which God made humanity. It is not meant to make people feel hopeless; it is meant to make reality plain before God. When this truth is seen clearly, the Bible’s answer in Christ becomes clearer, deeper, and more precious.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because people may compare themselves to others and miss that God’s own glory is the standard. If this doctrine is blurred, people either minimize what God warns about or carry burdens Christ came to answer. The result is confusion instead of repentance, fear instead of faith, or pride instead of humble dependence on the Lord.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Let this humble you without destroying you. Christ restores people who have missed the mark and teaches them to live for God’s glory again. Keep the language simple when teaching it: name the truth, point to Christ, and show the next faithful step. This helps the wounded, the new believer, the person in recovery, the church-hurt, and the teacher hear doctrine as light from God rather than cold information.
